sense: a judgement of quality or value

evidence: Cic. Q. Fr. 1.1.43: existimātiōnibus ac jūdiciīs
terms.comment: Properly a trial or a verdict, then any considered judgement; also judgement as a faculty, taste (Lewis & Short). See also opinion.

terms.gloss: a valuation, an assessment of worth
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.2.53: potestās omnis aestimātiōnis habendae (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 323 (aestimāre, evaluate a student’s work)
terms.comment: Properly a valuing in money, an appraisal, and in law the assessment of damages (lītis aestimātiō); then esteem and worth (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a judgement, an opinion; (modern) a review
terms.comment: A judgement or opinion, and very often the opinion others hold of someone, his reputation (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: nōn est tibi hīs sōlīs ūtendum existimātiōnibus ac jūdiciīs quī nunc sunt hominum, sed iīs etiam quī futūrī sunt
phrases.english: you must not rely only on the judgements and assessments of the people living now, but also on those of the people to come

sources: Lewis & Short: judicium · Lewis & Short: aestimatio · Lewis & Short: existimatio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 323, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026). Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. review (written judgment of book, film, play, etc.).
